thread:
maria: FYI apiserver 503s in asia-south2, saw leader election flip 3x in ~2m and GPU attach backlog climbing. Not sure if it's network or etcd.

devin: grabbing etcd metrics now. raft leader change + term jumps. fsync latency spiked to ~200ms on two controlplane nodes.

oliver: also seeing a bunch of NAT SNAT exhaustion on node-pool-asia-south2-*. kube-proxy logs show TCP: connection tracking full.

tess: controller-manager went into OOMBackOff on cp-3, restarted twice. Event stream shows many persistentvolumeclaims stuck waiting for attach.

maria: deploy bot shows a canary rollout for model-serving v2 at 4176000000. Could the rollout have increased attach rate? @kube-deploy-bot any correlation?

kube-deploy-bot: automated-note: Canary rollout of model-serving/v2 started at 4175999950. 120 pods scheduled in asia-south2 over 90s. No previous errors during rollout plan.

devin: timeline matches. sudden spike in attach ops + increased API QPS from controllers reconciling PVs.

oliver: suspect path: burst of pod creations -> kubelet requests volumes -> cloud provider attach spawns operations -> control plane queue + NAT conntracking -> apiserver timeouts -> leader election jitter. Also GPU attach pacing may amplify.

maria: logs from apiserver:
```
I0321 10:01:12.345678 1 wrap.go:42] RequestHandler failed: Get \"/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods\": net/http: request canceled (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
E0321 10:01:13.123456 1 eviction_manager.go:223] eviction failed: failed to get pods: Get \"https://127.0.0.1:6443/api/v1/pods\": dial tcp 127.0.0.1:6443: connect: connection refused
```

tess: controller-manager stacktrace shows worker goroutines piling up on attach operation timeouts.

devin: etcdctl endpoint status across cluster shows leader bouncing between cp-1 and cp-4. wal fsync backlog correlates with NVMe write latency spike on cp-4.

oliver: confirmed cloud provider API also reported a small quota error around the same time: \"AttachVolume: rate exceeded\" for the GPU-backed volumes. Could be hitting per-region attach QPS limit.

maria: immediate mitigations: 1) pause canary rollout and scale down model-serving canary replicas in asia-south2 2) add a temporary NAT pool / increase conntrack on nodepools 3) move some attach ops to a different region if possible

tess: +1 on pausing canary. I've scaled down the canary by 80% already.

devin: I'm promoting an etcd IOPS emergency job: increase fio throttle on cp-4 to warm the NVMe cache, and bump etcd compaction/defrag schedule to relieve WAL tail. Also opening a cloud support ticket for AttachVolume QPS.

oliver: increased conntrack on node pools and added two additional NAT IPs for asia-south2. Watching connections.

sre-oncall-bot: incident-alert: apiserver-503 spike detected in asia-south2. Severity: P1. Paging oncall.

maria: thanks. watch CPU/io on cp-4 and apiserver latency. If leader flips again revert cp-4 and cordon to force a stable leader on cp-1/cp-2 for now.

devin: leader stabilized after NVMe warm-up and scale-down. apiserver 5xxs dropping back to baseline. Attach backlog reduced to ~12 pending (was 180).

tess: controller-manager recovered, OOMBackOff cleared after kube-controller-manager restarted with richer GC flags. We'll add a longer-term fix: staggered pod startup for model-serving and pre-attach placeholder volumes.

maria: follow-ups: - cloud ticket for AttachVolume QPS + request temporary quota bump - plan controlled startup for large GPU fleets (stagger + prewarm) - monitor etcd fsync P50/P99 and NVMe latency alarms - add runbook step to throttle mass canary rollouts per region

devin: also propose adding a lightweight attach-cache controller that serializes attach ops per-node to avoid thundering herd.

oliver: cost note: temporary NAT IPs and higher NVMe IOPS will increase monthly spend. ops OK with emergency spend to restore SLAs; we'll track on the incident cost center.

maria: agreed. I'll tag finance and create cost estimate. Good job everyone, closing alert after 30m of stable metrics. :thumbsup:
